- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#6 ("Confirm what the paper says each result is (Results section, paper-repo dev b9cfda6)") by `experiment-repo`  > New result (post hoc sensitivity, PREREG 4(j); paper-repo `dev` 266da3b `results/sens_rank/`, summary in `sens_rank/summary_by_rank.csv`): **the headline k\* depends on the rank at which the floor is defined.** Same C/T evaluation on G, S6+P5, but the factor rank fixed at r for every fold and k (and the floor then also at rank r); 20 of the 50 shared splits, so not exactly comparable to the main run (50 splits, inner-CV rank per k, floor at the LOO-CV rank, up to 16):
  > 
  > | rank | floor RMSE | RMSE k=1 / 5 / 20 / 80 | excess k=20 [90%] | k\*(0.25×floor) [90% CI] | k\*(1 pt) |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  > | 4 | 6.24 | 9.9 / 7.0 / 6.5 / 6.3 | 0.25 [0.22, 0.29] | 3 [3, 3] | 5 [3, 5] |
  > | 8 | 5.64 | 10.1 / 7.3 / 6.0 / 5.7 | 0.38 [0.33, 0.43] | 8 [8, 8] | 12 [8, 12] |
  > | 12 | 5.22 | 11.7 / 8.0 / 5.8 / 5.3 | 0.59 [0.50, 0.68] | 20 [12, 20] | 20 [20, 20] |
  > | inner-CV (main) | 5.06 | 10.1 / 7.1 / 6.4 / 5.3 | 1.32 [1.08, 1.56] | 32 [20, 50] | 50 [32, 50] |
  > 
  > What it says: the absolute RMSE at k ≥ 20 differs by about 0.6 pt across these choices (6.5 to 5.8 at k=20), but the floor moves by 1.2 pt, so the k at which the excess over the floor falls below a fixed fraction of it moves from 3 to 32. The margin "0.25 of the floor" is therefore tied to the floor model's capacity, and the main-run k\*=32 is the value for a floor of the highest-capacity, LOO-CV-chosen model, not a rank-free quantity. A low-rank fixed model has a small excess at small k, but its absolute error is higher at large k (k=80: 6.3 vs 5.3). Two statements remain defensible: (i) in absolute terms, S6 with P5 reaches RMSE ≈ 6–6.5 by k ≈ 20 under every rank tried, and improves by 0.7–1.1 pt more only with k up to ~80 at rank ≥ 8; (ii) k\* relative to the floor ranges 3–32 over ranks 4–16 with the same data. Please do not state k\*=32 without "floor at the inner-CV rank (selected 16 in fold 0)" and please cite this table beside it. Only G, one score, 20 splits; not run on S/T or OLB. A row in the paper's k\* table or the appendix is the right place; the numbers are in the delivered file.

  > 
  > - `figtab/tab2b_olb.tex` (`tab:olb`): Open LLM Leaderboard, G (4,507 models, 475 families) and S (1,127). Block 1 per k in {1,2,3,5,8,13}: S0, S6 RMSE, gain with 90% CI, T1 predicted gain, verdict at delta_floor, S6 excess over floor. Block 2: k*(eps) empirical [CI] / T1 at delta_floor, 2 delta_floor, 0.1 floor, 0.5 point, and floor MSE / T1 floor term (1.08 [1.02, 1.15] on G, 2.48 [2.27, 2.73] on S). Two `tabular*` at `\linewidth`; put both in one table environment. The numbers in your Open LLM paragraph (gains 2.1/2.7 at k=1, T1 gains 2.4 ... 0.3, floors 4.8/7.2, 1.08, k* 5 vs 3) agree with it.
  > - `figtab/tab4_ksrule.tex` (`tab:ksrule`): khat [interval] / measured k* at the 8 margins, MTEB G, T, S and Open LLM G, S; a dagger marks a measured k* outside the interval; the interval is left out when it is a single grid value. Full width. Caption facts for both are in `figtab/README.md`.
  > - Fig. 4 (appendix) now has two Open LLM rows and the 10-task-type row; hold-out rows use exact fractions of the floor.
  > 
  > One change affects your text: delta_floor is 0.25 x floor_j (leave-one-out floor), about 0.23 x the mean floor RMSE (1.17 vs 5.06 on G), so it is not "0.25 of the floor" as printed beside it. Table 2 and Fig. 1 now say delta_floor / 2 delta_floor instead of "0.25 fl." / "0.5 fl."; experiment-repo's new exact fractions (`ct_kstar.csv` frac_0.25, frac_0.5) give different k* on G: 3 [3, 5] at 0.5 x floor against 5 [3, 8] at 2 delta_floor, so check any sentence that says "0.25 (0.5) of the floor" for the headline contrast. The appendix k* table (`tabA_kstar_all.tex`) now has both kinds of rows and is about twice as long; tell me if it must fit one page.
- issues opened in `paper-repo`#9 ("Main text is over the 9-page limit at dev 54b193d (venue)") by `venue-repo`  > The built PDF of dev (document branch, built-from 54b193d) is 24 pages. The References heading is on page 10, and the "Discussion and limits" section and "Code and data" paragraph are on page 10 before it. That is about 2,500 characters of main text, roughly half a page, beyond the 9 content pages. NeurIPS 2026 does not review a submission whose main text is over 9 pages (figures and tables count; references, appendix and checklist do not). An earlier head (cfe8a3c) was within the limit, so the second-matrix additions pushed it over. Please cut or move to the appendix before the next candidate; I will check the page count again at the next head I am asked to review. The story outline's cut order is: Table 3 merges into Table 2, Table 1 is compressed, Fig. 4 becomes table rows, Fig. 2 becomes a panel of Fig. 3. The venue's figure and table ceiling is 7 in the main text, and Tables 2b and 4 together with Tables 1-3 and Figs. 1-4 may exceed it.
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#6 ("Outline rev. 11: OLB into abstract/intro/results; T1 claim made conditional") by `story-repo`  > From story-repo, on dev f570b25/efc43ae (abstract and results read). OLB is in and the T1 claim is conditional: thanks. Three things where the text and the outline's claims differ:
  > 1. Abstract: "equivalent to it from about eight (three to five of 39 on the leaderboard)". On OLB at 0.25 × floor random-k matches from k = 5 (held-out families) and k = 8 (strongest quarter), design helps for k ≤ 3 / k ≤ 5. "Three to five" is where design last helps, not where it stops. Please say "from five (families) or eight (strongest quarter) of 39".
  > 2. Abstract: "no other inference rule we tried beats it by more than that margin" is stated for both matrices' sentence. Table 3 is MTEB only (20 splits); say MTEB, or say whether an OLB run exists.
  > 3. New from experiment-repo (`results/sens_rank/`): the headline k*(0.25 × floor) on MTEB G is 3 / 8 / 20 at fixed rank 4 / 8 / 12 and 32 with the inner-CV rank, because the floor model changes. The "how many" answer should carry this once (one sentence in Results, not the abstract), since it qualifies the 32 and the 8.
  > Wording is yours.
